title: Crematorium funding, accessibility upgrades and firefighter contract
subtitle: Also covered: grant funding results, joint municipal services update, and community recognition of local athletes and volunteers.
overview: Council approved $850,000 in additional funding from the Cemetery Reserve Fund to continue building upgrades and replace the existing retorts at Parkview Crematorium {{vote:m4}}. Staff said the cremation service is paid for by revenue rather than property taxes, so the decision should not change the tax levy.

Council accepted the facility accessibility audit report and asked staff for an annual update on accessibility improvements at City-owned facilities {{vote:m3}}. It also approved the grant update report {{vote:m5}}, received the 2022 Joint Services Initiatives Committee update as information {{vote:m6}}, and approved a settlement with the Waterloo Professional Fire Fighters Association covering January 1, 2023 to December 31, 2026 {{vote:m7}}.

As routine business, Council enacted the by-law that puts in place the zoning change for a daycare at 372 Erb Street West, which Council had dealt with on April 3 {{vote:m8}}. A closed session on council orientation was held before the public meeting. Members closed by recognizing local youth hockey teams and Volunteer Appreciation Week.

decisions.detail: Council approved $850,000 more from the Cemetery Reserve Fund to continue building upgrades and replace the existing retorts at Parkview Crematorium {{vote:m4}}.
Council approved the audit report and directed staff to provide an annual update on accessibility improvements at City-owned facilities {{vote:m3}}.
Council approved terms of settlement with the Waterloo Professional Fire Fighters Association, Local 791, for 2023 to 2026, and authorized the Mayor and Clerk to sign related documents {{vote:m7}}.
Council approved the grant update report, which reviews the City's grant applications and results {{vote:m5}}.
Council received the 2022 update on joint projects with neighbouring municipalities as information {{vote:m6}}.

debate: A delegate supported the funding request but urged the City to look at greener options than cremation and traditional burial, such as promoting green burial, human composting and water-based cremation. One councillor noted provincial hurdles to some of these options.

Councillors asked about emissions from cremation. Staff said the new unit would be more energy-efficient and that one unit would replace two older ones. They said the crematorium is a small share of the City's facility emissions, though high relative to its size, and that heat recovery was considered and set aside.

Councillors asked why the City runs a service that private businesses also offer. Staff said the cemetery and crematorium together give a one-stop service, that demand and prepaid arrangements remain strong, and that the building could be used for niche space if the market changes.

On accessibility, staff said the audits found far more need than the funding set aside, and that they would seek grants and pair work with planned construction. Councillors asked about in-house trades staff, staff needs, service counters and asset management planning.

On grants, councillors noted the work involved in large applications and asked how Council could help. Staff said they involve Council and others as needed and welcomed more advocacy to other levels of government.
